subject.title: fix(matrix): tolerate SAS accept events missing method

question: Should OpenClaw accept this private matrix-js-sdk Rust crypto preprocessor hook for Matrix SAS missing-method compatibility after live proof is provided?
rationale: The code is a focused bug fix, but it normalizes E2EE verification events at a private dependency boundary where ClawSweeper cannot safely infer permanent product/security ownership.

options.title: Accept Hook After Live Proof
options.body: Require redacted live Element/Synapse proof first, then merge the narrow compatibility hook with future matrix-js-sdk upgrade rechecks owned by the Matrix area.

options.title: Reject Private Hook
options.body: Pause this PR and pursue an upstream matrix-js-sdk or Matrix SDK-level compatibility fix instead of relying on a private backend field.

options.title: Override Proof And Own Risk
options.body: A maintainer may explicitly override the proof gate and accept the private-hook risk, but that leaves the live user path unproven on this branch.

recommendation.title: Accept Hook After Live Proof
recommendation.body: Require redacted live Element/Synapse proof first, then merge the narrow compatibility hook with future matrix-js-sdk upgrade rechecks owned by the Matrix area.
